title: In-Console Usage Insights (Beta) — Internal GTM One-Pager (Draft)
content:
INTERNAL ONLY — Redwood Inference GTM Enablement (Draft)

Feature name
- In-Console Usage Insights (Beta)

One-liner
- “Understand and reduce LLM spend with a route + model cost breakdown, top cost drivers, and exportable reports — directly in the Redwood Console.”

Why this matters (customer pain → our answer)
- Customers can’t easily answer: “What endpoints are driving cost?”, “Which model/variant is most expensive?”, “What changed since last week?”, “Why does my bill spike when latency rises / cache misses happen?”
- Today they stitch together logs, ad hoc warehouse queries, and invoices. It’s slow, error-prone, and hard to share with Finance/FinOps.
- Usage Insights puts cost attribution at the same place developers debug performance (Console), with totals that are designed to reconcile with billing.

Target users & buying centers
- Engineering leads / platform teams: want fast, accurate breakdowns to prioritize optimization work.
- FinOps / Finance partner: wants exports and consistent totals vs invoice for chargeback and budgeting.
- Solutions engineers: need a credible story for “cost transparency” during evals (especially Dedicated/Private prospects).

Positioning & differentiation
- Production-grade attribution (route + model) with explainable cost drivers (tokens, cache, retries, fallbacks, context distribution) built for real-world inference behavior.
- Not just charts: “what changed?” insights and direct links to levers (batching/caching/routing guidance) so teams can act.
- Designed for enterprise expectations: RBAC for cost visibility + audit logging for exports.

What’s included in Beta (scope)
1) Cost & usage breakdown tables
- Breakdown by API route + model (optionally filtered by workspace/project, environment, deployment mode, region, time range).
- Metrics called out explicitly:
  - Tokens in / tokens out
  - Cache hit / miss (where applicable)
  - Retries + fallbacks attribution (where telemetry supports)
  - Streaming overhead indicators (where applicable)
  - Latency context to correlate spend with performance

2) Top cost drivers + “What changed?”
- A ranked view of routes/models driving spend.
- Change detection: e.g., token out increased WoW; model mix shifted; cache hit rate dropped.
- Explanation strings suitable for copy/paste into Slack/Jira.

3) Exports + shareable reports
- CSV export for breakdown views (async export for larger ranges; signed downloads).
- Shareable link behavior (RBAC-aware). NOTE: exact behavior may be limited in early beta depending on security sign-off.

4) Data freshness indicators
- Shows freshness timestamp and warnings if data is partial/lagging.

What’s NOT included (explicitly out of scope for initial release)
- Automated optimization actions (we provide recommendations/links, not “one-click fix”).
- Scheduled email reports.
- Fully custom customer-defined dimensions beyond the supported set.

Ideal customer fits / when to lead with this
- Large or fast-growing usage where endpoint sprawl exists (many routes, multiple models, multiple workspaces/projects).
- Customers asking for:
  - “cost by endpoint/route”
  - “export to finance / chargeback”
  - “reconcile vs invoice”
  - “what changed” weekly reporting
- Strong hook for Dedicated + Private prospects who need transparency and governance.

Talk track (AE/SE)
- “Redwood Usage Insights lets you pinpoint spend at the route + model level — not just a single total. You can see what changed, export reports for Finance, and tie cost back to the drivers that matter in inference (tokens, cache, retries, fallbacks, context length).”

Discovery questions (to qualify + tailor demo)
- “Do you need cost allocation by team/project/workspace?”
- “Which endpoints are most important to you (chat, embeddings, rerank, OpenAI-compat)?”
- “How are you reconciling usage totals with your invoice today?”
- “Do you have RBAC requirements around who can see cost or export data?”
- “Do you need route breakdown for VPC/private deployments and/or region-specific reporting?”

Demo flow (recommended)
1) Start at Overview: show Top cost drivers (last 7 days) and a clear route + model table.
2) Drill into a single route:
   - Show tokens in/out, cache hit rate, retries/fallbacks, and context length distribution.
   - Show “what changed?” narrative.
3) Export CSV:
   - Download + show file naming + columns.
   - Mention signed URL + audit logging.
4) Close with next steps:
   - Identify 1–2 routes to optimize.
   - Point to docs on caching/batching/routing.

Screenshots (placeholders)
- [Screenshot Placeholder #1] Usage Insights landing page: Top cost drivers cards + “What changed?” summary
- [Screenshot Placeholder #2] Route + model breakdown table with filters (project/env/time)
- [Screenshot Placeholder #3] Drill-down detail view (tokens, cache hit/miss, retries/fallbacks, latency)
- [Screenshot Placeholder #4] Export modal + “Export ready” state + signed download link
- [Screenshot Placeholder #5] Permission denied state (RBAC) + help text

Beta enablement + rollout notes
- Gated behind feature flag + allowlist.
- Enablement requests: use internal process (see INT request template) and confirm account owner approval.
- Expectation setting: early beta may have limits on long time ranges, high-cardinality routes, and partially missing route tags for certain streaming endpoints/regions if instrumentation rollout is incomplete.

Known limitations to proactively mention
- Data freshness: near-real-time but not instantaneous; console shows freshness timestamp and partial-data warnings.
- Long time ranges: 30-day queries may time out in early beta; recommended to start with 7d/14d and use export for longer windows.
- Route normalization: dynamic paths are templated; edge cases exist for OpenAI-compatible endpoints and legacy routes (work in progress).
- Model aliases: model family/version bucketing is designed to reduce confusion, but alias-related duplicates may appear in early iterations (we’re tightening bucketing rules).

FAQ (for AEs/SEs)

Q: How is “cost” calculated here? Is it the invoice amount?
A: It’s usage-attributed cost based on Redwood metering + pricing hooks, designed to reconcile to billing totals within a defined tolerance. Differences can occur due to rounding, timing windows, credits/discounts, and late-arriving events. The console will show freshness/lag indicators.

Q: Can customers use this for chargeback?
A: Yes for engineering-driven chargeback (route/model/project). For formal finance workflows, we recommend CSV export + their BI tool. We’re prioritizing consistent totals and stable dimensions.

Q: Who can see cost data? Can we restrict it?
A: Yes. Cost views are RBAC-gated and can be restricted at the workspace level (e.g., hide cost for non-finance roles). Exports and share links are permissioned and audited.

Q: Does this work for Dedicated and Private deployments?
A: Yes, as long as the underlying telemetry is available in the workspace/project. For Private/VPC, data residency/retention policies apply; export controls may be stricter for restricted workspaces.

Q: What’s the story on exports (security)?
A: Exports are generated server-side. Downloads are via signed URLs and are audit-logged (who exported, what scope, when). We also enforce throttling/limits to reduce data exfil risk.

Q: What dimensions can I filter by?
A: Time range, workspace/project, environment, route, model; optional filters include deployment mode and region where supported.

Q: What does “route” mean (and how do you avoid cardinality blowups)?
A: Route is a canonicalized endpoint path (templated IDs / path params). We apply normalization rules and guardrails to prevent high-cardinality explosions. When normalization fails, events may fall into an “unclassified/other” bucket until fixed.

Q: Do “retries” count as spend?
A: Retries that result in actual inference work are counted (they consume tokens/compute). We’ll surface retry-related drivers so customers can reduce them (timeouts, bad client behavior, fallback policies).

Q: Can we show the customer exactly “what changed” week over week?
A: Yes in the UI for common patterns (token out increase, cache hit drop, model mix shift). We should present it as heuristic-driven guidance, not a financial audit statement.

Competitive notes (internal)
- Generic cloud dashboards often show overall spend or per-service totals; they don’t connect inference-specific drivers (tokens/cache/fallbacks) to specific routes/models in a developer-friendly console.
- Some inference providers expose raw usage logs but lack explainable deltas + built-in export governance.

Objection handling
- “We already have billing exports.”
  - Response: Billing exports are necessary but not sufficient; they lack route-level engineering context and inference drivers. Usage Insights bridges Finance + Engineering with consistent attribution.
- “We can do this in our warehouse.”
  - Response: Many customers can, but it’s costly to build/maintain and hard to keep correct with changing models/runtimes. Our built-in views are continuously updated with serving semantics and governance.

Customer proof points (early)
- HelioChat: wants weekly cost-driver reporting and internal chargeback by route.
- Northstar Fintech: RBAC + audit logging + reconciliation expectations.
- AcmeAI: explicit requirement for route/model breakdowns + CSV export for finance.

Internal contacts / escalation
- Product (requirements/positioning): Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes
- SE enablement + customer feedback: Markus Klein, Evan Scott
- DevEx/docs: Alex Martinez, Elliot Price
- Finance/reporting alignment: Rishi Malhotra
- Security/RBAC/audit: Marcus Lin

Next steps (for GTM)
- Collect 3–5 beta screenshots once UI stabilizes.
- Create a short “demo checklist” for SEs (filters + a sample route drilldown).
- Align language in pitch deck + website (post-beta) with DevEx terminology (route vs endpoint).

Notes to self (draft)
- Confirm final naming: “Usage Insights” vs “Cost Insights” (DevEx prefers “Usage Insights” to avoid confusion with invoice).
- Ensure we have a single sentence explaining reconciliation and why invoice totals can differ (credits, discounts, timing).
- Add a small appendix with CSV column definitions once export spec is final.
